equity_bridge.item: FY2025 final dividend HK$0.35/share paid 3 July 2026, after the 30 June balance date
equity_bridge.note: HK$304,074k = US$38,803k per H1 FY2026 interim report note 12 (1415.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:1879). The price is ex this dividend, so the cash is no longer the buyer's.
FY2025 AR balance sheet line 4664 (US$5,303k); charged once here, flows left consolidated

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: average of the base-case first three forecast years (14%, 5%, 0%). Every historical CAGR is a step-change artefact (Apple rear-camera share gains took revenue from US$924m in FY2023 to US$3,500m in FY2025) and none is a usable forward rate.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 23.8% vs revenue 36.1% and EPS 35.0%: >30% relative divergence. Revenue growth outran book because FY2020 paid a US$150m special dividend off a smaller base and because the business runs on thin EMS margins (net margin 5.6%) so revenue scale converts to equity slowly.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2020 79.7, FY2021 35.8, FY2022 -4.5, FY2023 20.1, FY2024 -197.9, FY2025 217.6. The 3-yr owner-FCF CAGR is undefined (FY2022 base negative) and the 5-yr figure (22.3%) is below the reported-FCF 24.4% because SBC rose from US$0.06m to US$16.1m and interest income from US$1.6m to US$8.5m over the period. Cumulative FY2023-25 owner FCF is just US$40m on US$6.9bn of revenue: the capacity build for the Apple share gain consumed nearly all the cash the gain generated, which is why the valuation rests on a component-built mid-cycle margin rather than on any historical FCF series.

scenario_narratives.base: Cowell keeps its rear/flip-chip camera-module allocation at its single anchor customer (Apple, via the Luxshare/Luxvisions ecosystem that controls ~70% of the company) through the current flagship cycle: FY2026 revenue +14% on H1's +18%, a +5% FY2027, then a flat FY2028 as one product cycle pauses, and ~2-3%/yr content-driven growth after that. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin holds at ~9% as gross-margin erosion from the volume-module mix is offset by scale and AI-driven manufacturing efficiency; capex settles at 3-3.5% of revenue after the FY2024 capacity build; cash tax ramps from the 15% HNTE rate to 18% with withholding and Pillar Two. Owner-FCF margin matures at ~4.5%, terminal value capped at 12x for a cyclical single-customer supplier. No credit for the AR/VR, smart-glasses, robotics or automotive optionality.
scenario_narratives.bull: The January 2026 reshuffle of Apple's rear-camera supply chain hands Cowell further main-camera share, Pro/Pro Max optical content keeps rising (periscope, larger sensors, computational photography modules), and at least one adjacent market (AI smart glasses or automotive/robotics vision) becomes a second revenue leg: growth of 18%/12%/8%/8% through FY2029 before fading to 3%. Mix and operating leverage lift pre-SBC EBITDA to 10.5% (still below the FY2021-22 11-12% level), capex runs at 4% while capacity is added, and the terminal cap is 14x in recognition of a partly diversified customer base.
scenario_narratives.bear: The concentration risk crystallises: Apple re-sources or in-sources part of the rear-module programme, or tariff/technology-control escalation against a Dongguan-based supplier to a US brand forces a share loss. Revenue +8% in FY2026 (H1 already banked) then -15% and -12% across FY2027-28 before stabilising at ~2% growth, i.e. revenue settles ~US$2.8bn, still three times FY2023. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin compresses to 7% on under-absorbed capacity and customer price pressure with no hedge against RMB/KRW costs; capex falls to maintenance 2.5%; terminal cap 10x. Related-party supply and labour agreements with Luxshare leave minorities with limited control over how the downturn is shared.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Cowell as a thin-margin, single-customer EMS component supplier on a mid-cycle owner-FCF margin built from components, not on the FY2025 cash flow, which sits on a trough capex year and a working-capital release and is roughly six times the FY2023-25 average. The step-change in revenue from Apple rear-camera share gains is treated as real and largely retained (base), but the customer, jurisdiction and governance concentration are charged in the flows through a 30% bear weight and a 12x terminal cap, not through a padded discount rate. Net cash of US$294m (after the July dividend and NCI, ~US$250m or HK$2.2/share) is the one hard asset in the valuation.
key_risks_to_valuation: Loss of share or in-sourcing at the single anchor customer: revenue is order-driven with no diversification buffer, and the bear case assumes a 25% peak-to-trough revenue decline that history (FY2017-18: -28%) shows is realistic

The mid-cycle capex assumption: capex ran 8-10% of revenue in FY2022-24 and 2-3% in FY2025-H1 FY2026; if the next product qualification needs another FY2024-scale build, owner FCF margin drops below 2% for that year
US-China tariff and technology-control escalation against a Dongguan-based supplier to a US brand, flagged explicitly by the Chairman
Related-party supply, labour-services and machinery agreements with the Luxshare/Luxvisions controller: pricing is not demonstrably arm's-length, and a 70% controller limits minority recourse
Margin squeeze from memory/storage component inflation or customer price-downs on a 10% gross margin with no FX hedging of RMB/KRW costs
HNTE 15% tax status renewal and PRC dividend withholding tax on repatriation of the Dongguan cash

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (HKEX regular close); 52-week range 19.90-35.04; USD/HKD from Yahoo HKD=X the same day

sanity_check_note: scripts/sanity_check.py applies inputs.fx_rate backwards for currency-mismatched tickers (known systemic bug, not fixed in this run): the historical_table shows FY-end prices of 8.6-237.6 where the real HKD prices were HK$1.1-30.3 converted to US$0.14-3.86, so every printed historical P/B, EV/EBITDA and P/Sales is inflated ~fx^2 = 61.6x and the implied multiples ~fx = 7.8x. Hand-bridged on a consistent USD basis at the HK$21.50 quote (US$2.74, market cap US$2,432m, EV US$2,182m after the July dividend and NCI): P/E 12.0x FY2025 (13.4x SBC-adjusted, 10.7x TTM), P/B 3.0x on June-2026 equity, EV/EBITDA 7.1x FY2025 (7.5x SBC-adjusted, 6.8x TTM), P/Sales 0.69x. Historical range (printed table / 61.6): P/B 0.35x (FY2018) to 5.6x (FY2024), EV/EBITDA ~3x to ~20x, P/Sales 0.2x to 1.9x. At the weighted IV of HK$20.86 the implied multiples are P/E 13.0x adj, P/B 2.9x, EV/EBITDA 7.3x adj, P/Sales 0.67x: inside the historical range and at or below the FY2024-25 levels, so passed: true is the right verdict, reached via the backwards arithmetic. No driver change made.

inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares for H1 FY2026 (887,717,000; interim report note 7(b)). Issued shares 868,981,800 at 30 June 2026 less ~8m treasury shares held by the share-award trustee, plus in-the-money options (weighted exercise price US$0.56 vs ~US$2.74 price). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice.
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 June 2026 interim balance sheet (US$'000): bank loans 133,840 current + 8,004 non-current = 141,844; lease liabilities 4,922 + 29,245 = 34,167 (treatment A, in net debt); cash 403,963; bank deposits >3 months 66,071; no pledged deposits. Net debt = 141,844 + 34,167 - 403,963 - 66,071 = -294,023. Ties to the filing's own -56.7% gearing ratio. The FY2025 final dividend (paid 3 July 2026, after balance date) is deducted in equity_bridge, not here.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report cash flow reconciliation, 'Equity settled share-based payment expenses' US$16,100k (1415.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:5878). No cash taxes on net-share settlement disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0 every year), so no combined figure to prefer; add-back used as-is.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income US$8,494k stripped from the base because net cash (US$294m) exceeds 1x the owner-FCF base; the cash pile is added back once in the bridge.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 purchases for the share-award scheme US$24.2m (FY2024 US$7.8m); nil in H1 FY2026. The flat count is being funded in part by repurchases, but the award-scheme buybacks are the delivery mechanism for SBC and are already charged via the SBC expense.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in USD; HKEX quote in HKD. USD/HKD 7.848 (Yahoo HKD=X, 2026-10-16), i.e. model-currency value x 7.848 = HKD value. The HKD is pegged in a 7.75-7.85 band so the bridge moves <1% in either direction; no dual listing to parity-check against. The FY2025 final dividend of HK$0.35/share = US$0.0446/share confirms the direction (x7.848 HKD per USD).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are USD, so WACC is built from USD inputs: 10-yr UST ~4.1% risk-free, 5.0% equity risk premium, beta ~1.3 for a single-customer EMS component supplier = ~10.6% cost of equity; net cash so cost of debt is irrelevant. Rounded to 10.5% (the house USD operating-company default). No ad-hoc premium for customer concentration or China-manufacturing risk: those are charged ONCE, in the flows, via the bear scenario path and its 30% weight. Same WACC in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: A: leases as debt. Lease liabilities (US$34.2m) sit in net debt; lease principal (US$5.0m FY2025) and interest (US$1.8m) are NOT deducted from the flows, and right-of-use renewal is immaterial (US$0.9m H1 FY2026 additions) against US$49-74m/yr owned-asset capex. Leases are ~1% of EBITDA; the treatment choice is worth <US$0.01/share.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; NCI book value US$5.3m (FY2025, loss-making subsidiaries) deducted once in equity_bridge. NCI share of profit is -US$2.0m FY2025, so attributable profit slightly exceeds consolidated; immaterial either way.
inputs.tax_note: Cash tax rate anchored at 15%: the Dongguan operating subsidiary is a High and New Technology Enterprise taxed at 15% (FY2025 AR note 5), the Pillar Two 15% global minimum applies from 2025, and the 5% PRC dividend withholding tax applies on repatriation. FY2025 effective P&L rate was 12.0% (US$26.9m on US$223.8m PBT) and cash tax paid US$41.4m (18.5%) as prior-year provisions caught up; H1 FY2026 P&L rate 14.6%. Ramped to 18% by year 4 to carry the withholding tax and HNTE renewal risk.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (USD flows vs HKD quote, lease treatment A, NCI in bridge, interest income stripped with the cash pile in the bridge, risk charged once). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2: an operating company (camera-module manufacturer), non-US filer, highly cyclical with a single customer's product cycle. First valuation of this ticker; no prior DCF or memory entry. EBITDA margin paths are PRE-SBC (FY2025 reported EBITDA 8.7% + SBC 0.46% = 9.2%) so that owner EBITDA after the SBC line ties to the reported 8.7%; FY0 NOPAT at 9.2% - 0.46% - 1.9% D&A, taxed at 15%, is ~US$204m against reported attributable profit of US$194.9m, within non-operating noise (net interest ~-US$5m, tax at 12%). FY2025 owner FCF of US$217.6m is NOT the base the projections compound from: it sits on a trough capex year (US$74m after US$248m in FY2024) and a US$50m+ working-capital release; the component build gives a 3.6-4.5% owner-FCF margin, versus 6.2% reported in FY2025 and ~0.4% averaged over FY2023-25. Price at a regular HKEX close; not an after-hours print.

base.growth_note: FY2026 +14%: H1 was +18% and management's own H1 profit pre-announcement was met, but the memory/storage cost squeeze on iPhone demand flagged by the Chairman and a tougher H2 FY2025 comparative (H2 FY2025 revenue US$2,140m, +37%) argue for a softer second half. FY2027 +5% then a flat FY2028 encodes one normal product-cycle pause; thereafter ~GDP-plus content growth, no diversification credit.
base.margin_note: Pre-SBC EBITDA held at 9.0-9.2% (FY2025 9.2%, H1 FY2026 9.3%). Gross margin has fallen every year since FY2021 (15.1% -> 10.2%) as the mix shifted to high-volume rear modules; opex leverage has offset that at the EBITDA line. No further expansion assumed in the base.
base.capex_note: Capex/revenue averaged 6.2% over FY2022-25 (US$496m on US$8.0bn revenue) during the capacity build, versus 2.1% in FY2025 and 3.1% in H1 FY2026. 3.5% near term, 3.0% mature, roughly in line with D&A ramping to 2.8% as the FY2024 flip-chip equipment depreciates through.
base.wc_note: Manufacturer: receivables US$404m + inventory US$218m exceed payables US$513m by US$109m at June 2026 (US$197m at Dec 2025), 3-6% of revenue. Growth therefore consumes cash; -5% of the revenue change.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30% because this is the clearest single-customer dependency in the folder (96.7% of trade receivables from one customer, 99.9% from five) layered on a single-jurisdiction manufacturing base exposed to US-China trade policy and a controlling shareholder that transacts with the company on both sides of the ledger; any one of those is a bear trigger on its own. Bull trimmed to 25% because it needs two independent things to go right (further Apple share gains AND a second end-market reaching scale). Base 45%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
